The slice I'd designed
New files

src/MyRestaurant.Domain/Orders/OrderNarrative.cs — a pure fold giving the guest's view of a line, including removed ones, with price-adjustment old→new history and a GuestMayRemove that mirrors §6.5.3 exactly. Sibling to OrderProjection, held in step by a test asserting its non-removed lines equal OrderProjection's. (written)
src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Orders/OrderStaging.cs — the pure basket: stage/unstage/quantity, mark-for-removal, PruneRemovals (so a stale tick can't sink an all-or-nothing batch), Build(IIdentifierFactory) returning operations plus parallel descriptions for the rejection panel. (written)
src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Orders/MoneyText.cs — RESTAURANT_CURRENCY_CODE-driven formatting, since ToString("C") would silently ignore the configured code. (written)
Components/Pages/Table/TableOrderSurface.razor — the interactive-server island. (designed, not yet written)
Two test files.
Modified: TableJoin.razor (hosts the island — the page stays [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting] static SSR for the cookie/redirect work, and the island carries the live parts), TableArea.razor, app.css, docs/DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md (F-36).

Two findings worth flagging now:

F-36 — timestamps ignore RESTAURANT_TIME_ZONE. Every surface uses .ToLocalTime(), which is the server process zone; your container sets no TZ, so guests would see UTC. §13 also never settles 12- vs 24-hour. I'd record it and fix every surface in one dedicated slice rather than leaving two conventions on one page.
A closed-then-reopened sitting on the same table makes GetOpenSittingForMemberAsync return the new sitting — the settled-view check has to compare identifiers, not just null-ness.
Say "continue" and I'll write the remaining files and produce the tar.gz in one go.

M4 Slice 2 — the guest ordering surface. Extracts at repo root:

tar -xzf myrestaurant-m4-slice-2.tar.gz -C /home/kushal/src/dotnet/myrestaurant
cat docs/_append/BUILD_PROGRESS-m4-slice-2.md >> docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md
rm -rf docs/_append
Files to delete: none. The only removal is docs/_append/ after you concatenate it (BUILD_PROGRESS.md is ~1,400 lines; regenerating it whole would be mostly noise).

Path	
src/MyRestaurant.Domain/Orders/OrderNarrative.cs	new
src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Orders/OrderStaging.cs	new
src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Orders/MoneyText.cs	new
.../Components/Pages/Table/TableOrderSurface.razor	new
.../Components/Pages/Table/TableJoin.razor	replaced
.../Components/Pages/Table/TableArea.razor	replaced
.../wwwroot/app.css	replaced (appended section)
docs/DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md	replaced (F-36)
3 test files	new
No migration, no packages, no DI change — AddRestaurantOrders() already registers everything the island resolves.

The three decisions worth your veto
An interactive island inside a static page. /table/{id} keeps [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting] for the cookie and redirect work; TableOrderSurface renders with @rendermode="InteractiveServer" for the live half. The roster moved into the island too — §9 sends SittingMemberJoined to table members and a static list can't hear it. TableJoin.razor's inline <style> is gone; .table-* moved to app.css, since an inline style in one component silently styling another's markup is an invisible dependency.

Every read scoped by the sitting, not the table. GetOpenSittingForMemberAsync is the one table-keyed query, and its answer is discarded unless it names this sitting. Without that comparison, a closed-then-reopened table would swap the order under the reader mid-session; with it, the same event does what §11.1 asks and flips to the settled bill.

A second fold, and a test against drift. OrderNarrative keeps removed lines (the opposite of order_current_line) because §11.1 wants them struck through with actor and reason, and the "old" side of a price arrow is stored nowhere — it's what the fold was holding when the adjustment arrived. Since OrderProjection now has a sibling, NonRemovedLines_AgreeWithOrderProjectionOnARandomisedSequence closes the triangle §8.5 opened.

F-36, recorded not fixed
Every surface uses ToLocalTime(); RestaurantOptions.ResolveTimeZone() has no caller and the container sets no TZ, so a deployed instance shows guests UTC. I kept the existing convention here rather than putting two time formats on one screen — the static header and the island are one page. The fix needs a decision §13 never made (12- vs 24-hour), so it wants its own slice before M5.

Build risk is concentrated in TableOrderSurface.razor — first interactive island in the tree, first <select>, lambda-bound @onchange inside a @foreach, nested record in @code. I avoided Dictionary/HashSet collection expressions and pattern-variable definite assignment across Razor's generated control flow, but that's the file to watch. Send me dotnet build output if it complains.
